correctness.rationale: The scalar covariance map is Möbius with one positive and one negative fixed point. Conjugation by t(P)=(P-p)/(P-m) gives exact multiplication by rho=F'(p). Direct algebra shows three-point Aitken on the Möbius orbit maps t to (rho t)^2. For |a|<=1, P1>=q>(p+m)/2 forces -1<t(P1)<0, so every squared projective error lies in (0,1), yielding strict upper bounds decreasing to p while the raw sequence increases below p. For every |a|>1, h=r=1 and 0<q<a^2-1 give the exact negative extrapolate -q(q+1)/(a^2-1-q). The packaged verifier checks the symbolic identity and rational witnesses.

value.rationale: Steady-state covariance is a central numerical quantity in Kalman filtering, and conservative covariance bounds are operationally meaningful. The theorem turns three ordinary scalar Riccati iterates into a certified lower/upper bracket without solving the algebraic Riccati equation, explains the acceleration by exact projective squaring, and identifies a sharp structural boundary where the same extrapolation can become an invalid negative covariance. This is a natural reusable fact rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
